dedupe_keys.name: berkeley lab residential indoor air quality databases california homes and apartments

description: Berkeley Lab's Residential Building Systems Group lists three open indoor air quality datasets from California housing on its IAQ databases page, each archived on Dryad under CC0. The first covers 70 detached houses built in 2011 to 2017 to meet California's mechanical ventilation rules, each monitored for a week with windows closed: time-resolved indoor and outdoor fine particles, indoor formaldehyde and carbon dioxide, time-integrated NO2 and NOx, cooktop, range hood and fan operation, and airflow and leakage tests. The second covers 23 low-income apartments in four properties built or renovated in 2013 to 2017, all with gas cooking, where range hood and bathroom fan airflows were lower than specified and only eight met all ventilation code requirements. The third holds R code and PM2.5 data for a random forest method that finds indoor emission events, using 836 events in 18 apartments and 65 new homes. Datasets were published in April, October and December 2020. Coverage: California. Caveats: each home was measured for about one to two weeks, so long-term exposure is not captured. Access: free download from Dryad. Useful for ventilation, health and energy retrofit analysis and planning; related records are not yet linked.
